summary.text: A 77-year-old woman, ASA IV with a known penicillin allergy, was admitted after diagnosis of a non-recent subcapital right femur fracture for right hip hemiarthroplasty. Her history included type 1 von Willebrand disease, immune thrombocytopenia with a baseline platelet count of 40,000/μL, splenic non-Hodgkin lymphoma in remission after six cycles of R-CHOP, colorectal cancer treated with sigmoidectomy, stroke, hypertension and other comorbidities, and she took ten regular medications.

On admission she had pancytopenia with a platelet count of 12,000/μL and was considered unfit for surgery. One platelet pool was transfused, Hematology and Transfusion Medicine were consulted, and a presumptive diagnosis of ITP was made. Prednisolone 60 mg per day was started and surgery postponed. Given hemostatic vWF and factor VIII levels, it was decided there was no need to transfuse these factors.

After seven days of corticotherapy the platelet count improved to 64,000/μL and she was cleared for surgery. The next day she received tranexamic acid 1 g and a platelet pool and underwent non-cemented hip hemiarthroplasty under balanced general anesthesia with stress-dose hydrocortisone, clindamycin prophylaxis, an arterial line and a femoral nerve block. Estimated blood loss was 300 mL, hemoglobin fell from 7.9 to 7.2 g/dL, and one unit of red cells was given.

Postoperatively she was monitored in a Level 2 intensive care bed and received tranexamic acid 500 mg IV every eight hours for 24 hours. She had no apparent bleeding but received one unit of red cells on day one and two more on day two, and low-molecular-weight heparin was started on day three. On day eight postoperatively hemoglobin was 8.7 g/dL and platelets 44,000/μL, and she was discharged clinically stable. The discussion describes a positive outcome with no life-threatening hemorrhage.
